claims.text: Pulumi programs can reference existing Terraform state files (the guide taught how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi).
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs (the guide taught how to use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs).
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly in Pulumi.
HCL code can be converted to Pulumi code.
Terraform and Pulumi deployments can be orchestrated together (as covered in this guide).

The `@pulumi/terraform` package exposes a `terraform.state.S3Reference` class that takes `bucket` and `key` arguments to reference a Terraform state stored in S3 (also referenced as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` in the Automation API example).
`terraform.state.S3Reference` instances expose a `getOutput(name)` method that returns outputs from the referenced Terraform state.
`new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` with `getOutput("vpcId")` retrieves an output from another Pulumi stack; the core stack shown exports `vpc`, not `vpcId`.
A core infrastructure stack containing a VPC could be managed by Terraform while the application stack is managed by Pulumi and consumes its outputs.
The `aws.ecs.Cluster` resource accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` (value `"DEFAULT"`) properties.
`pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
State ownership can be transferred from Terraform to Pulumi gradually, resource-by-resource.

The `pulumi import` command syntax takes a resource type token, a resource name, and a cloud provider ID (e.g., `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`, `aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet`, `aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster`).

A user-written helper class can use Terraform state reference outputs to import all resources of a given type via a 'Pulumi import API' (the example implies Pulumi has an import API callable from a program).
Pulumi policies (Policy as Code / CrossGuard) can implement infrastructure policies that work across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.

The `@pulumi/policy` package exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`, and policies use `name`, `description`, `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"`, and `validateResource` with a `(resource, args, reportViolation)` callback signature.
The `aws.s3.Bucket` resource has an `acl` property that can be `"public-read"` or `"public-read-write"`, and a policy can read it to block public buckets.
The Automation API lets you embed Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.
The `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` module exports `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack` accepting `stackName`, `projectName`, and an inline `program` function.
The Automation API `Stack` object provides `setConfig(key, { value })`, `up({ onOutput })`, and the result of `up` exposes an `outputs` property.
Pulumi component resources can wrap Terraform-integrated infrastructure so that the complexity of multi-tool management is left to the platform team rather than development teams.
A `pulumi.ComponentResource` subclass calls `super(type, name, {}, opts)` and `registerOutputs(...)` with `ComponentResourceOptions` for the constructor options.

The `aws.lb.LoadBalancer`, `aws.ecs.TaskDefinition`, and `aws.ecs.Service` resources accept the arguments used in the example (`loadBalancerType`, `internal`, `subnets`, `requiresCompatibilities`, `networkMode`, `cpu`, `memory`, `containerDefinitions`, `launchType`, `networkConfiguration.assignPublicIp`, `desiredCount`).
Developers can create WebApplication component resources in Pulumi without knowing they depend on Terraform-managed resources.
